content.value_statement: Long AI projects lose decisions and working context across sessions. This skill provides structured guidance for capturing, compressing, storing, and restoring project knowledge.
actual_capabilities: Guides extraction of project metadata, architectural decisions, dependencies, and semantic tags.
Describes structured context models using JSON Schema and hierarchical representations.
Outlines snapshot versioning, context drift detection, and selective restoration workflows.
Compares storage formats including JSON, Markdown, Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, and YAML.
Provides strategies for compression, vector retrieval, and knowledge graph organization.
limitations: Provides guidance and illustrative snippets, not a complete executable context management system.
Does not include the referenced implementation playbook or working vector database connectors.
Requires users to identify and exclude secrets or sensitive project information.
Does not define measurable accuracy guarantees for compression or semantic retrieval.

use_cases.title: Prepare Developer Handoffs
use_cases.description: Capture architecture, active decisions, dependencies, and unresolved work before another developer or agent continues the project.

use_cases.title: Maintain Agent Session Continuity
use_cases.description: Design repeatable snapshots that preserve essential project state between Claude, Codex, or Claude Code sessions.

use_cases.title: Organize Institutional Knowledge
use_cases.description: Structure project history for searchable storage, semantic retrieval, and later onboarding.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Minimal Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal context snapshot for [project]. Include the goal, current state, key decisions, open tasks, and important file locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a short record before ending an AI session.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Structured Context Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a standard context capture plan for [project]. Cover metadata, architecture, dependencies, decisions, risks, tags, storage format, and restoration steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a consistent context format across sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Context Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the context snapshots from [earlier date] and [later date]. Identify changed decisions, dependencies, assumptions, risks, and unresolved conflicts.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project owner needs to understand how project knowledge changed.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Retrieval Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a comprehensive context architecture for [project]. Include serialization, fingerprints, versioning, compression, vector retrieval, access controls, validation, and recovery testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced team is planning a durable multi-agent knowledge system.

output_examples.input: Create a minimal snapshot for a payment service migration.
output: Goal: Move payment processing without interrupting checkout.
Current state: The new provider works in staging.
Key decision: Use a gradual traffic rollout.
Open work: Complete failure testing and rollback approval.

output_examples.input: Compare two architecture snapshots for context drift.
output: Changed decision: Event delivery moved from polling to webhooks.
New dependency: A managed message queue now handles retries.
Unresolved conflict: Retention requirements differ between documents.
Recommended action: Confirm retention policy before deployment.

output_examples.input: Recommend a storage approach for shared project context.
output_examples.output: Use versioned Markdown for reviewed decisions and structured records for automated retrieval. Exclude secrets and validate each snapshot before restoration.

best_practices: Capture rationale and unresolved questions, not only final decisions.
Exclude credentials, personal data, and confidential values before storing context.
Version snapshots and test restoration after significant project changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated summaries as authoritative without project owner review.
Do not store complete repositories when a focused context record is sufficient.
Do not compress context until important constraints and decision rationale disappear.

faq.question: Does this skill save project files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for designing context capture and storage workflows.

faq.question: Which storage formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It discusses JSON, Markdown, Protocol Buffers, MessagePack, and YAML.

faq.question: Can it support vector databases?
faq.answer: It outlines integration concepts for Pinecone, Weaviate, and Qdrant, but it does not provide working connectors.

faq.question: How should sensitive information be handled?
faq.answer: Exclude secrets and sensitive data before capture, then apply access controls appropriate to the storage system.

faq.question: Can it compare context across sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. Its guidance includes versioned snapshots, fingerprints, semantic differences, and context drift detection.

faq.question: Is the included Python ready for production?
faq.answer: No. The snippets are illustrative and depend on undefined extraction, analysis, tagging, and compression functions.
